summary: Lula won the Oct 25 runoff, and Brazil has now fallen four days in a row: the Ibovespa lost 1.06% to 169,186 on Oct 29 and the dollar rose 0.76% to R$5.39 on worries about Lula's spending plans (Agencia Brasil, Reuters via TradingView). The central bank decides Nov 3 to 4 with the Selic at 13.75%. Before the vote, economists expected a 0.25 point cut in November (Focus survey, Oct 23); since the result, rate futures jumped and analysts now debate a pause or even a hike, so sources disagree on what is priced (UOL, Estadao, InfoMoney). In New York on Oct 29 EWZ fell 1.43% to 33.14, BBD 3.66% to 2.63, and NU rose 0.67% to 12.05 (Massive). The test is still a credible spending plan from Lula's team before the decision.
for_you: No Brazil buys, swings or new puts until the Nov 3 to 4 decision. NU closed at 12.05 on Oct 29, 8.0% under its 13.10 'thesis broken' line, and stays Wait. An EWZ Nov 20 $37 put is 10.4% in the money at 33.14; with no verdict, do not roll.

watch.name: Real per US dollar
watch.why: Up 0.76% on the day on fiscal worries (Agencia Brasil).

watch.name: Selic policy rate
watch.why: Cut 0.25 point on Sep 16. Next decision Nov 3 to 4. Pre election Focus survey expected another 0.25 point cut; after Lula won, futures jumped and a pause is now widely discussed (Folha, Estadao). A pause or hike instead of a cut hurts banks and fintech lenders.

watch.name: Ibovespa
watch.why: Down 1.06%, a fourth straight loss after the election (Agencia Brasil).

watch.name: Presidential runoff
watch.why: 64,256,232 votes to Flavio Bolsonaro's 59,826,041 (TSE). One report says Flavio dropped his annulment request a day later (SBS); his Liberal Party accepts the count (TRT World). Inauguration is Jan 5, 2027 (CBS).

watch.name: IPCA inflation, 12 months
watch.why: September reading, above the 4.5% ceiling of the target range. Makes fast Selic cuts less likely.

changes.what: Brazil's central bank cut the Selic by 0.25 point to 13.75% in a unanimous vote, its first cut right before an election in two decades. Lower rates help banks, lenders and retailers.
First round vote: Flavio Bolsonaro 47% to Lula 45%, against polls that had Lula ahead. Runoff set for Oct 25.
Brazilian assets rallied on the result. Ibovespa up 7.7% to a record 206,912, the real up about 4% to 5.00 per dollar, Bradesco ADR up about 19%, Itau about 15%, Nu about 12%, MercadoLibre about 9%.
September inflation came in at 0.82% for the month and 4.58% over 12 months, above the 4.5% ceiling. The Ibovespa still closed at a new record of 209,067 as runoff polls favored Bolsonaro.

AtlasIntel's runoff poll for Bloomberg (Oct 3 to 8, 5,026 people, released Oct 9) gives Flavio Bolsonaro 52.8% of valid votes to Lula's 47.2%, wider than Datafolha's 52% to 48%. Bolsonaro rose from 47.4% to 51.1% of total votes since Atlas's last poll, breaking the earlier tie.
changes.for_you: Markets already price a Bolsonaro win, so the poll mostly lowers the odds of a shock. Still no new Brazil swings or puts into the Oct 25 runoff. PBR is left out of both lists: a new government could change its pricing policy either way.

changes.what: The runoff is tightening. Quaest (Oct 10 to 13, 2,154 people, released Oct 14) has Flavio Bolsonaro at 51% of valid votes to Lula's 49%, and O Povo reports Datafolha (Oct 13 to 15) at the same 51% to 49%, down from 52% to 48% earlier and inside the 2 point margin of error. EWZ fell 2.4% to 41.58 on Oct 15.
changes.for_you: Brazilian banks rallied on a Bolsonaro lead that is now inside the margin of error. NU is 'Buy zone now', but wait for the Oct 25 result before acting.

changes.what: A Futura/100% Cidades poll released Oct 16 has Flavio Bolsonaro at 50.8% of valid votes to Lula's 49.2%, a technical tie inside its 2.2 point margin. An average of eleven pollsters is 51.6% to 48.4%, with nine showing Bolsonaro ahead, while Polymarket (77%) and Kalshi (78%) gave Bolsonaro much higher odds as of Oct 16 (Rio Times). EWZ rose 0.6% to 41.83 on 1.58x volume and NU fell 1.2% to 14.56 (dashboard).
changes.for_you: No action until after Oct 25. Betting markets are far more confident than the polls, so a Lula win is the bigger surprise and would likely hit NU, ITUB and BBD hardest; a Bolsonaro win is mostly priced. All are left out of both lists because the result is still a coin flip in the polls. NU (14.56) is 'Buy zone now' but wait for the vote.

changes.what: A Vox Brasil poll of 2,100 voters taken Oct 15 to 17 has Lula at 51% of valid votes to Flavio Bolsonaro's 49%, the first recent poll with Lula ahead (Rio Times). Datafolha (Oct 13 to 14) still has Bolsonaro 51% to 49%, and all recent polls are inside their margins of error. Betting markets were far more confident in Bolsonaro (77% to 78% on Oct 16), so the gap between polls and prices is the risk.
changes.for_you: No action until after Oct 25. NU (14.56) is 'Buy zone now', but a Lula win would likely hit NU, ITUB and BBD, while a Bolsonaro win is mostly priced. All are left out of both lists because the polls are a coin flip.

changes.what: AtlasIntel (reported Oct 19) has Flavio Bolsonaro at 49.8% to Lula's 47.6%, or 51.1% to 48.9% of valid votes, down from a 5.4 point lead on Oct 9; Nexus for BTG Pactual has 46.5% to 45.9%. Prediction markets still give Bolsonaro about 77% (Polymarket) to 80% (Kalshi), so polls are tighter than prices.
changes.for_you: No action until after Oct 25. NU (14.56) is 'Buy zone now' (zone 14.03 to 15.08), but a Lula win could hit Brazilian banks hard in a day. All four are left out of both lists while the race is this close.

changes.what: Polls published Oct 20 mostly lean to Flavio Bolsonaro: Real Time Big Data (Oct 15 to 19, 2,000 voters) has 52% to 48% of valid votes, Gerp 53% to 47%, Alfa 51.5% to 48.5% and Instituto Franca 50.8% to 49.2%, while Data Ranking has Lula 50.4% to 49.6%. The Ibovespa rose 1.57% to 208,295.98 and the real firmed to about 5.02 per dollar.
changes.for_you: No action until after Sunday's vote. NU closed 15.09 on Oct 20 (Yahoo), just above its 15.07 zone top on Oct 19 data. Markets already price a Bolsonaro win, so a Lula win is the bigger move; no Brazil puts before Monday.

changes.what: Quaest's runoff poll released Oct 21 has Flavio Bolsonaro at 45% and Lula at 44%, down from 46% to 44% on Oct 14 (Reuters). With four days to go, the race is within one point, while markets have priced a Bolsonaro win.
changes.for_you: No buys or puts on NU (15.05 on Oct 21, right at its 15.05 zone top) until after Sunday's vote. A Lula win is the bigger surprise for Brazilian banks.

changes.what: Final polls before the Oct 25 runoff show a dead heat: Datafolha has Flavio Bolsonaro and Lula at 50% each of valid votes (released Oct 22, down from 51% to 49% a week earlier), and PoderData has Flavio at 51% to 49% (released Oct 22, down from a 4 point lead). Markets have priced a Bolsonaro win, so a Lula win is the bigger surprise.
changes.for_you: No NU buys or puts before Monday. NU is 'Buy zone now' at 14.73 on Oct 22 (zone 14.11 to 15.03). If Lula wins and NU gaps toward 14.11, that is the level to watch; if Flavio wins, wait for the gap to settle.

changes.what: On the last trading day before the Oct 25 runoff, the Ibovespa rose 0.47% to 205,082.56 and the real strengthened about 0.9% to 4.993 per dollar (Agencia Brasil via Rio Times, Oct 23). Polymarket priced Flavio Bolsonaro at 76.9% to win, well above what the roughly 51% to 49% poll average implies, and EWZ closed at 42.59 on 2.27 times normal volume (dashboard).
changes.for_you: No trades before Monday. Prices lean to a Flavio win, so a Lula win would likely hit EWZ, ITUB, NU and PBR hardest; a Flavio win may bring only a small gain because it is expected. The tickers are left out of both lists because the result is a coin flip in the polls.

changes.what: The last polls before the runoff, released Oct 24, lean slightly to Flavio Bolsonaro: Datafolha 51% to 49% (from 50% to 50% on Oct 22), Quaest 51% to 49% and AtlasIntel 50.8% to 49.2% of valid votes, all inside their margins of error. Betting markets put him near 80%.
changes.for_you: No trades before Monday's open settles. If Lula wins and NU falls into its 14.13 to 15.02 zone, wait for a day when buyers lead before a small first buy; if Flavio wins and NU opens above about 15.32, do not chase. The tickers are left out of both lists because the result is not known.

changes.what: Lula won the Oct 25 runoff 51.79% to 48.21% (TSE), against polls and betting markets that favored Flavio Bolsonaro, who says he will seek annulment. On Oct 26 the dollar opened up 8.65% at R$5.425, a circuit breaker halted the Ibovespa, and in New York premarket EWZ fell 25.3% to 31.83, NU 23.6% to 11.57, PBR 23.6% to 19.98 and ITUB 25.6% to 7.19 (Benzinga, InfoMoney).
changes.for_you: No Brazil buys or puts today. NU fell through its 14.13 to 15.02 zone instead of into it, so Sunday's 'wait for buyers to lead' rule holds and the verdict will likely change tonight. An EWZ put sold last week is in the money; with no verdict, do not roll.

changes.what: Oct 26 closes: the Ibovespa fell 13.88% to 176,608.23 and the dollar rose 8.21% to R$5.4027 (InfoMoney, Exame); in New York EWZ closed down 19.8% at 34.15, NU 17.0% at 12.59, ITUB 20.4% at 7.70, BBD 28.0% at 2.93, PBR 14.0% at 22.50 and MELI 7.8% at 1668.72 (dashboard). Markets now price a Selic hike in November (InfoMoney). One report says Flavio Bolsonaro dropped his annulment request (SBS), and his party accepts the count (TRT World).
changes.for_you: NU is now Wait, below its 13.10 'thesis broken' line: no buy. EWZ closed 7.7% below a $37 put strike; with no verdict, no roll.

changes.what: Day two after the election crash: the Ibovespa slipped 0.51% to 175,710.05 on Oct 27 and the dollar fell 0.97% to R$5.3506 (Money Times). Citi moved Banco do Brasil to sell, citing farm loan quality and political risk (UOL). US closes on Oct 27: EWZ 34.30 (up 0.44% on 2.16 times normal volume), NU 12.40 (down 1.51%), ITUB 7.67, BBD 2.91, PBR 22.30, MELI 1680.51 (Massive).
changes.for_you: No action. NU stays under its 13.10 line; wait for the Nov 3 to 4 rate decision. EWZ is left out of both lists: the real recovered but stocks did not.

changes.what: Day three of the post election sell off: the Ibovespa fell 2.68% to 171,006.10 on Oct 28 while the dollar slipped 0.19% to R$5.34 (InfoMoney, UOL). US closes on Oct 28: EWZ 33.62 (down 1.98% on 2.08 times normal volume), NU 11.97 (down 3.47%), ITUB 7.40, BBD 2.73 (down 6.19%), PBR 22.03, MELI 1673.09 (Massive). AGCO reported Brazil tractor retail sales down 17% in the first nine months of 2026.
changes.for_you: No action. Heavy volume on a down day is distribution; NU is further under its 13.10 line. Wait for the Nov 3 to 4 rate decision.

changes.what: Day four of the post election slide: the Ibovespa fell 1.06% to 169,186 on Oct 29 and the dollar rose 0.76% to R$5.39 (Agencia Brasil). Correction to earlier entries: the pre election Focus survey expected a Selic cut in November, and after the vote analysts debate a pause; a hike is one view, not the consensus (Folha, Estadao). US closes Oct 29: EWZ 33.14, NU 12.05, ITUB 7.37, BBD 2.63, PBR 21.90 (Massive).
changes.for_you: No action. NU is 8.0% under its 13.10 line. The real weakening again is the warning sign; wait for Nov 4.
